To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
100 of the 188 chemicals we tested bound to the ER, while 88 were ER non-binders, and that 4-benzoxyphenol,2,4-dioxybenzophene, and 2-2'-methylene bis(4-chlorphenol) are new ER-binding chemicals.

we have determined the ER relative binding affinies of 188 natural, synthetic, and xenochemical compounds, including 2,4- dihydroxybenzopheno, 4-benzoxyphenol, and 2-2'-methylene bis(4- chlorophenol), and that we have determined a number of structural features that are important for ER binding.
the majority of the 100 chemicals tested bind to the ER and that the ER RBAs of 188 natural, synthetic, and xenochemical compounds range from 1 x 106 to 0.01.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of standardized, in vitro assays that are used to determine ER affinity for a broad spectrum of chemicals, and the subsequent utilization of these data to assess the potential for chemicals to interact with the ER.
the identification of chemicals that have estrogenic activity and the characterization of their ER-binding affinity.
the development of a comprehensive data base on ER binding affinities for a large group of chemicals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a large number of chemicals, including many xenochemicals, bind to the ER and may therefore exert estrogenic or antiestrogenic effects in the body.
the ER is an extremely promiscuous receptor, binding with high affinity to a wide range of chemicals with diverse structures.
a chemical binds to the ER if it exhibits an RBA of 1 or greater.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more hydrophobic the chemical, the higher the ER affinity.
a large number of natural chemicals and xenochemical categories bind to the ER and that these chemicals exhibit a broad range of RBAs.
the ER is a promiscuous receptor that binds to an extremely diverse array of chemicals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ER can bind a wide range of structurally diverse chemicals.
a chemical's structural features, as well as its overall size and charge, are important factors in determining ER binding.
the ER has a high degree of chemical selectivity, and that the ER has affinity for a large group of structurally diverse chemicals.
